requirements.title: The format specifier supplies a format specification or list-directed formatting
requirements.definition: The format specifier supplies a format specification or specifies list-directed formatting for a formatted input/output statement.

pending.format-specifier-supplies-format-specifi: Use a formatted internal WRITE to a character buffer initialized to # with FMT="(SS,I2)" and value 7; expect exact " 7" and IOSTAT zero, proving the specifier supplies explicit formatting.
pending.format-specifier-supplies-list-directed-: Use a list-directed internal WRITE with FMT=* to a buffer initialized to # and a nondefault integer value; assert only successful transfer and properties owned by list-directed formatting, not processor-dependent spacing.

requirements.oracle: Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans establish a non-default state first (for example by writing known records, initializing variables to nonzero/nonblank sentinels, or using a compile-only conforming control) and then observe only portable properties: exact internal records, successful IOSTAT zero, nonzero IOSTAT or named status values where the standard names them, required INQUIRE tokens, or required diagnosis of a numbered syntax rule or constraint. Negative/source-control plans change one property from the conforming control and do not require a particular diagnostic message, severity, exit status, or printed rule number.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Source accounting only. requirements.title: Format syntax admits default character expressions, FORMAT labels, and asterisks
requirements.definition: A format is a default character expression, the label of a FORMAT statement, or an asterisk.

pending.default-character-expression-format-form: Compile/run an internal WRITE using FMT="(SS,I1)" and a sentinel-filled buffer; a syntax negative deletes the expression operand only.
pending.format-statement-label-form: Compile/run a WRITE using FMT=100 with a same-scope `100 FORMAT(SS,I1)` and sentinel buffer; the paired syntax negative keeps C1232 premises but removes the label token.
pending.asterisk-format-form: Compile/run a list-directed internal WRITE using FMT=* with nondefault input; the paired syntax negative replaces `*` with an otherwise invalid token.

requirements.title: FORMAT labels identify same-inclusive-scope FORMAT statements
requirements.definition: A label used as a format shall be the label of a FORMAT statement, and that FORMAT statement shall appear in the same inclusive scope as the statement containing the FMT= specifier.

pending.format-label-targets-format-statement: Diagnostic/control pair changes only the target of FMT=100 from a same-scope FORMAT statement to a same-scope CONTINUE branch target; the conforming control is otherwise identical.
pending.format-label-same-inclusive-scope: Diagnostic/control pair keeps a labelled FORMAT statement but moves it to a different inclusive scope, for example an internal procedure, while the control keeps `100 FORMAT(SS,I1)` in the same inclusive scope.

requirements.title: Character-expression formats evaluate to valid format specifications
requirements.definition: A default character expression used as a format shall evaluate to a valid format specification as described by 13.2.1 and 13.2.2.

pending.character-expression-valid-format-specif: Positive plan writes through FMT="(SS,I1)"; source-control negative changes only the runtime character value to a malformed format such as "(Q)". Because this unnumbered rule has no required diagnostic by itself, a fixture would observe only successful valid transfer or nonzero status where later format rules require it.

requirements.title: Array character-expression formats concatenate elements in array element order
requirements.definition: If a default character expression format is an array, all elements are treated as specified in array element order and concatenated.

pending.format-array-elements-concatenated-in-ar: Use a character array such as ["(","SS",",","I1",",","I1",")"] as FMT for internal WRITE of 3 and 4 to a sentinel buffer; expect the same exact result as FMT="(SS,I1,I1)", and mutate element order to make the format or result differ.

requirements.title: Asterisk format makes the statement list-directed
requirements.definition: If the format is an asterisk, the statement is a list-directed input/output statement.

pending.asterisk-format-makes-list-directed-stat: Use FMT=* in an internal WRITE of initialized values and assert only behavior fixed by list-directed rules after they are registered; do not assert processor-dependent spaces or widths from this classification facet.

review_rationale: Source registration for 12.6.2.2-12.6.2.16, the individual io-control-spec specifiers (batch160). Every unit hash-verified by independent reviewers across two rounds. Each temporary mode specifier is split into its value restriction, its one-statement effect with restoration of the connection mode (observed by INQUIRE after the statement), and the omitted-means-unchanged rule. Round 1 found a pending plan expecting exact output from I2 on a positive value without fixing the sign mode; it now uses SS, and a sweep found no other plus-, leading-zero- or rounding-dependent exact output. R1215 and C1232 were pre-accounted. Source accounting only.
